en.title: Fresh snow in the US West: 11 in in 72 hours at Mt Baker (6 November)
en.description: Mt Baker got 11 in (27 cm) of new snow in the last 72 hours, 4 in (11 cm) of it in the last 24 hours. It now has about 19 in (47 cm) on its upper …
en.lede: Mt Baker got 11 in (27 cm) of new snow in the last 72 hours, 4 in (11 cm) of it in the last 24 hours. It now has about 19 in (47 cm) on its upper slopes, according to our snow model.

p: Elsewhere, Buttermilk, Dutch Henry Ski Hill and Ski Cooper got 6 in (15 cm), 6 in (15 cm) and 6 in (14 cm) in the last 72 hours.
Our snow model shows 82,506 sq mi (213,690 km²) of snow-covered ground in the US West today, with snow at 140 of 195 resorts.
At about 4,367 ft (1,331 m), Mt Baker has 6 in (14 cm) today; a normal 6 November has 4 in (10 cm) there.
Only one winter in ten has more than 26 in (66 cm) on this date.
A week ago the same spot had 7 in (18 cm).
In past winters the best snow at Mt Baker usually came late March / early April.
An early lead like this matters most for the lower and middle runs, which usually wait until December for this much snow.
Day by day at Mt Baker: Friday 6 November 4 in (11 cm); Saturday 7 November 2 in (6 cm); Sunday 8 November 10 in (25 cm); Monday 9 November 1 in (2 cm).

Height by height at Mt Baker: 3,629 ft (1,106 m) 2 in (5 cm) on the ground, 1 in (2 cm) more in the next 7 days; 4,367 ft (1,331 m) 6 in (15 cm) on the ground, 6 in (16 cm) more in the next 7 days; 5,105 ft (1,556 m) 10 in (25 cm) on the ground, 9 in (22 cm) more in the next 7 days.

The Chepeta station (10,489 ft / 3,197 m) measured 20 in (51 cm) of snow on the ground on 1 November, with 12 in (30 cm) of new snow in 24 hours. The Red Mountain Pass station (11,060 ft / 3,371 m) measured 24 in (61 cm) of snow on the ground on 1 November, with 11 in (28 cm) of new snow in 24 hours. The Bison Lake station (10,951 ft / 3,338 m) measured 15 in (38 cm) of snow on the ground on 1 November, with 10 in (25 cm) of new snow in 24 hours.
Keep in mind: resort values come from our snow model and describe an area, while stations measure one point.
Height matters: at Mt Baker, our model gives 10 in (25 cm) at the top (5,105 ft / 1,556 m), 6 in (15 cm) at mid-mountain (4,367 ft / 1,331 m) and 2 in (5 cm) at the base (3,629 ft / 1,106 m).
At Mt Baker, the freezing level reaches 4,003 ft (1,220 m) to 9,449 ft (2,880 m) on 6 November, above the top of the resort (5,105 ft / 1,556 m): rain or wet snow is possible on every slope that day.
Until 9 November, our forecast gives 13 in (33 cm) at Mt Baker.
Forecasts a few days ahead can change: look at the map again the day before you travel.
After fresh snow, wind builds drifts on sheltered slopes. Off-piste, the first days after a snowfall need the most care.

advice: Fresh snow is best in the first hours after it stops: go early, before the sun and the crowds.
Look for snow high up and on north-facing slopes: they keep it longest, while south-facing slopes lose it first in the sun.
Before you ski off-piste or go touring, read the official avalanche bulletin (links below).
Snow on the map does not mean a resort is open: check lifts and opening dates on the resort's website.
Get a powder alert in the SnowScope app to know when Mt Baker gets fresh snow.
